body.statement: Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), under independent multinomial sampling and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\) when margins are estimated, the deterministic selector \(\widehat\chi_n\) chooses an incident first-order-compatible rigid chart and \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with probability tending to one. On these certified separated rigid charts, \(\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)\Rightarrow N(0,V_{\tau})\), and \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau}\). Because \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\), scalar contrasts and the elliptical branch of \(W_n\) have asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). If no chart is certified, the total procedure returns \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\), \(\widehat\tau_n=(0,0)\), \(\widehat V_n=I_2\), and \(W_n=[0,1]^2\), with no covariance-consistency or Wald-coverage assertion for that fallback branch.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(H\) be a compact subset of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\); every
uniform assertion below is over \(\zeta\in H\).  Under independent
multinomial sampling, the reduced selected-table coordinates are averages of
bounded categorical vectors.  In design A with estimated margins, the margin
coordinates are averages from an independent sample and
\(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).  Therefore a constant \(C_H<\infty\)
exists such that
\[
 \sup_{\zeta\in H}
 E_{\zeta}\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2^2
 \le \frac{C_H}{n}. \tag{56}
\]
The margin summand is zero when margins are known.  Markov's inequality gives
\[
 \sup_{\zeta\in H}P_{\zeta}
 \{\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2>\delta\}
 \le\frac{C_H}{n\delta^2},
 \qquad
 \widehat\zeta_n-\zeta=O_P(n^{-1/2}) \tag{57}
\]
uniformly on \(H\).

The selected-table covariance is
\(\operatorname{diag}(p^-)-p^-p^{-\top}\).  Independence and the relative
sample-size limit add the block
\(\lambda\{\operatorname{diag}(m^-)-m^-m^{-\top}\}\) when margins are
estimated, and no block when they are known.  These are exactly the blocks of
\(\Omega_{\zeta}\).  The multinomial central-limit and delta lemma yields
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)
 \Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_{\zeta}). \tag{58}
\]
The convergence is uniform on \(H\).  Indeed, from any sequence in \(H\),
compactness extracts a subsequence converging to \(\zeta_\star\).  For each
fixed vector \(u\), bounded categorical summands give the uniform expansion
\[
 E_{\zeta_n}\exp\{iu^{\top}\xi_{n,1}/\sqrt n\}
 =1-\frac{u^{\top}\Omega_{\zeta_n}u}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}). \tag{59}
\]
Multiplication of the selected and independently rescaled margin
characteristic functions, together with \(n/n_m\to\lambda\), proves (58)
along that subsequence.  The subsequence criterion proves uniformity.
Because the covariance formula is polynomial in the cell probabilities,
(57) and continuous mapping also give
\[
 \widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta} \tag{60}
\]
uniformly on \(H\).

For every \(\zeta\in H\), the incident set
\[
 \Gamma(\zeta)
 =\{\chi:d_{\chi}(\zeta)=0,
             \ \eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\} \tag{61}
\]
is nonempty.  Distance to a closed set is one-Lipschitz, so each
\(\chi\in\Gamma(\zeta)\) obeys
\[
 d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)
 \le\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2. \tag{62}
\]
There are finitely many labels and their normalized slack functions have the
continuous extensions required in \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\).  Compactness
therefore supplies \(\delta_H>0\) such that
\[
 \|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2<\delta_H
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \eta_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)\ge\varepsilon/2
 \quad(\chi\in\Gamma(\zeta)). \tag{63}
\]
Since \(t_n=n^{-1/4}\), (57), (62), and (63) show that some incident chart
passes both selector inequalities with probability tending uniformly to one.

Conversely, the closure of each incompatible chart is at distance at least
\(\varepsilon\) from \(\zeta\).  Hence
\[
 d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)
 \ge\varepsilon-\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2. \tag{64}
\]
On the event in which the last norm is below \(\varepsilon/2\), (64) exceeds
\(t_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\); no incompatible chart can pass.
The exhaustive atlas certification and lexicographic selection thus imply
\[
 \sup_{\zeta\in H}P_{\zeta}\{\widehat\chi_n=\bot
 \text{ or }\widehat\chi_n\text{ is not incident and first-order
 compatible}\}\longrightarrow0. \tag{65}
\]

On the complementary event, rigidity and first-order compatibility give
\[
 F_{\widehat\chi_n}(\zeta)=\tau,
 \qquad J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\zeta)=J(\zeta), \tag{66}
\]
where \(J(\zeta)\) is the common incident Jacobian.  The twice continuously
differentiable extensions, finite chart set, and compactness yield a common
Hessian bound.  Taylor's theorem, (57), and (66) therefore give
\[
 \widehat\tau_n-\tau
 =J(\zeta)(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)+R_n,
 \qquad
 \sqrt n\|R_n\|_2=o_P(1) \tag{67}
\]
uniformly on \(H\).  Combining (58) and (67) proves
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
 \Rightarrow N(0,J(\zeta)\Omega_{\zeta}J(\zeta)^{\top})
 =N(0,V_{\tau}). \tag{68}
\]

Continuity of the derivatives, (57), and (60) show that the raw sandwich
matrix
\[
 \widetilde V_n=
 J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)\widehat\Omega_n
 J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)^{\top}
\]
satisfies \(\widetilde V_n\xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau}\) uniformly.  Since
\(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\), Weyl's inequality gives
\[
 P_{\zeta}\{\lambda_{\min}(\widetilde V_n)>\varepsilon/2\}
 \longrightarrow1 \tag{69}
\]
uniformly.  Thus \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with probability tending to one,
and on that event \(\widehat V_n=\widetilde V_n\).  Hence
\[
 \widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau}. \tag{70}
\]

For any fixed nonzero contrast vector \(h\), the lower eigenvalue condition
and Slutsky's lemma give
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\,h^{\top}(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)}
      {(h^{\top}\widehat V_nh)^{1/2}}
 \Rightarrow N(0,1), \tag{71}
\]
so the corresponding two-sided scalar Wald interval has asymptotic coverage
\(1-\alpha\).  Likewise,
\[
 n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)^{\top}\widehat V_n^{-1}
   (\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
 \Rightarrow\chi^2_2. \tag{72}
\]
The true target belongs to \([0,1]^2\), so intersecting the ellipse with that
square does not change its coverage event.  Continuity of the chi-square law
at its displayed quantile proves coverage \(1-\alpha\) for the elliptical
branch, uniformly on \(H\).

Finally, if no chart is certified, the selector definition gives
\(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\).  The total-map definitions then give
\(F_{\bot}=(0,0)\), \(J_{\bot}=0\), and a zero raw sandwich matrix.  It is
not positive definite, so \(\widehat\gamma_n=0\), and the fallback clauses
give identically
\[
 \widehat\tau_n=(0,0),\qquad
 \widehat V_n=I_2,\qquad W_n=[0,1]^2. \tag{73}
\]
The consistency and Wald conclusions used the high-probability event (65),
so none is asserted for this fallback branch.
body.justification: The chart rule, covariance formula, and nonsingularity margin make regular-stratum Wald inference operational and falsifiable.
body.gap: The anchor and earlier response-type estimators establish regular-case normality only for their inverse formulas, not for deterministically selected rational and simple algebraic rigid charts.
body.consumer: Separated empirical tables obtain reproducible standard errors and Wald regions on every first-order-compatible atlas chart.
